Upstream: gpui-pre-windows 0.3.9 (crates.io), Zed snapshot 93d7456.

build.rs, src/directx_renderer.rs, src/shaders.hlsl and the added compile-shaders.ps1 differ from upstream. The patch supports WSL-to-Windows Release builds by invoking Windows D3DCompiler through PowerShell and generating the shader byte arrays that upstream's Windows-host-only build script produces. The native Windows build path is preserved. The runtime renderer lazily grows its path resolve/MSAA surfaces from 1×1 to the top-left rectangle covering clipped paths, in 128-pixel buckets. Resize resets them. Screen coordinates, full pixel resolution and 4× MSAA are preserved; the path sprite shader queries the actual texture dimensions for UV coordinates. Empty windows avoid unused surfaces, and narrow graphs avoid full-window allocation. Windows fixture screenshots and the resize budget regression script passed (about 68 MiB startup, 79 MiB after resize, versus 117/180 MiB with full-window surfaces). This bounds allocation demand; it does not prove the driver returns all freed allocations. Full-DAG, large-diff and long-session acceptance remains separate. ClearState/Flush was tested and removed because it did not reduce the retained memory.

Keep upstream LICENSE files. GPUI_POWERSHELL can override the default Windows PowerShell executable path. Debug Windows cross-builds are not supported by this patch because upstream debug rendering uses host source-file paths at runtime.
